description: Use when scheduling automated deletion of temporary records, enforcing data retention policies, running nightly cleanup jobs, reclaiming org storage, managing recycle bin, or performing async bulk deletion of aged records. Trigger keywords: batch delete, retention policy, purge records, cleanup job, recycle bin, emptyRecycleBin, hard delete, nightly purge, storage optimization. NOT for archiving records to Big Objects or external storage instead of deleting them — use data/data-archival-strategies. NOT for deleting unused fields, flows and other metadata — use admin/org-cleanup-and-technical-debt.
inputs: Object API name and retention period (e.g., purge records older than 30 days)
Whether permanent deletion (hard delete / emptyRecycleBin) is required
Expected record volume — determines batch size and chunking strategy
Cascade deletion risk: master-detail child objects that auto-delete with parent
name: batch-data-cleanup-patterns
official_sources: Best Practices for Deployments with Large Data Volumes (`salesforce_large_data_volumes_bp.txt`): soft deletion still affects performance; Recycle Bin items don't count against storage; no item limit; 15-day retention and no guaranteed purge time; Bulk API hard delete recommended (L733-742); hard delete for one million or more records (L1019-1023).

Apex Reference Guide (`salesforce_apex_reference_guide.txt`): `Database.emptyRecycleBin` is permanent, takes 10,000 records, cascade Ids must be excluded (account example), and counts against DML statements (L206900-206935); `Test.setCreatedDate` (L240831-240836).

Apex Developer Guide (`salesforce_apex_developer_guide.txt`, Winter '27 264; re-pointed 2026-10-20 from the 262 lines in parentheses, every value unchanged): test DML rolled back (L1007-1009; 262 L1008-1010); cron syntax and user time zone (L17017-17024; 262 L16812-16820); 100 scheduled Apex jobs (L17151; 262 L16947); five queued or active batch jobs (L17216; 262 L17012) and flex queue of 100 (L17436; 262 L17235); invoking batch from a trigger with extreme caution (L17932-17934; 262 L17731-17733); one execute per batch test (L17937-17938; 262 L17734-17737); 50 million QueryLocator rows (L17902; 262 L17701); default scope 200 and QueryLocator chunks up to 2,000 (L17510-17512, L17993; 262 L17309-17311, L17792).

Apex Developer Guide 264, Execution Governors and Limits (`salesforce_apex_developer_guide.txt`): 10,000 records processed by DML statements, `Approval.process`, or `database.emptyRecycleBin` per transaction, sync and async (264 L19759). The Winter '27 limits cheatsheet no longer carries the Apex tables and points to that section (`salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.txt` 264 L21-29); the earlier cite was cheatsheet 262 L66.

Bulk API 2.0 and Bulk API Developer Guide (`api_asynch.txt`): `hardDelete` skips the Recycle Bin; "Bulk API Hard Delete" permission off by default (L1640-1647); ingest workflow, batches upload, UploadComplete, and results resources (L161, L605-647, L698-734).

Metadata API Developer Guide (`api_meta.txt`): no deploy of a class with active jobs by default (L22218-22221); ApexClass `.cls-meta.xml` and `status` (L22231, L22271); `purgeOnDelete` only in Developer Edition and sandboxes, roll-up summary fields purged on Metadata API delete (L4234-4246, L4638-4640).
Salesforce Security Guide (`salesforce_security_impl_guide.txt`): deleting a record cascades to its field history (L4895-4896).

SOQL and SOSL Reference, "Date Formats and Date Literals" (fetched from https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/get_document_content/soql_sosl/sforce_api_calls_soql_select_dateformats.htm/en-us/262.0): `LAST_N_DAYS:n` starts at midnight n days ago and includes today; `LAST_N_YEARS:n` is calendar-year based and ends December 31 of last year.
outputs: Batch Apex class implementing Database.Batchable<SObject> with retention filter
Schedulable wrapper class with System.schedule() cron expression
Optional per-chunk emptyRecycleBin() call in execute() so deleted rows cannot be restored (Recycle Bin rows do not count against storage)
Error log or custom object record capturing partial-delete failures
